$b=$ {{constant}}"] [:db/add "39fa67c3-62a0-548a-8170-3fac475b3d2d" :question/worked-solution "Let $f(x)=2 x^{2} + 2 x + 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=4 x + 2
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(-1\right)=4 \left(-1\right) + 2=-2
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-2\right)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(1\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2} + \frac{3}{2}\\
\left(-2\right)y&=-x+\left(-1\right)+\left(-2\right)\\
x+\left(-2\right)y&=-3
\end{aligned}
$$

$b=$ {{constant}}"] ["2bc8c064-6ab5-517b-8592-dd4c397e6102" :question/worked-solution "Let $f(x)=\frac{x^{6}}{8} - \frac{7 x^{3}}{4} - 2$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{3 x^{5}}{4} - \frac{21 x^{2}}{4}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=\frac{3 \left(2\right)^{5}}{4} - \frac{21 \left(2\right)^{2}}{4}=3
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(3\right)}=- \frac{1}{3}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-8\right)&=- \frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{3}+\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+\left(-8\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{3} - \frac{22}{3}\\
\left(3\right)y&=-x+\left(2\right)+\left(-24\right)\\
x+\left(3\right)y&=-22
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $3$ and the constant is $-22$."] ["2bc8c064-6ab5-517b-8592-dd4c397e6102" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["2bc8c064-6ab5-517b-8592-dd4c397e6102" :question/answer-fields "6f398cc4-3378-5bcf-800a-e098b3f356cb"] ["2bc8c064-6ab5-517b-8592-dd4c397e6102" :question/answer-fields "a92ad403-2689-5286-93db-881c39c5c22e"] [17592186092240 :knowledge-point/questions "2bc8c064-6ab5-517b-8592-dd4c397e6102"]] "retractions" []}
